name: Patchwork Scooter
description: The cheapest motorized personal vehicle that still functions as advertised. A small electric scooter with a step-through frame, manufactured by a dozen different companies that all copy the same basic design. They're everywhere in Tier 1-2 — parked in clusters, locked to railings, abandoned when the battery dies. The name comes from the repair culture: every scooter is a patchwork of replacement parts from different manufacturers in different colors. A scooter that's all one color is either new or fictional.
cost: Φ80 new, Φ20-40 used, batteries Φ10 each
common_usage: Short-distance commuting, errands, the default vehicle of the urban poor.
story_hooks: A specific model of scooter battery is exploding — the knockoff manufacturer used unstable chemistry and thousands are in circulation
Scooter chop shops in the Gray Zone operate as a front for a communications network — messages are passed inside battery housings
physical_description: A compact electric scooter with a worn aluminum step-through frame, its original color long obscured by mismatched replacement panels in faded blacks, grays, and industrial blues. The deck is scuffed polymer, the handlebars wrapped in frayed grip tape or electrical tape. Visible wiring, a jury-rigged battery pack, and misaligned wheel assemblies from three different manufacturers mark it as a survivor of a dozen repair cycles.
